rationale: Across all systematically characterized cohorts of individuals with FBXO11 pathogenic variants (IDDFBA, OMIM #618089), complex congenital heart defects, structural congenital limb-reduction deficiencies, and progressive neurodegenerative courses have not been observed. Cognitive disability is neurodevelopmental and stable rather than degenerative, and major visceral/structural malformations are notably absent. Head circumference is normal in the majority of individuals (~70-75%), with mild microcephaly observed in only ~21-24% (4/19 in Gregor et al. 2018, 24% in Goel et al. 2026) and macrocephaly in ~10% (2/19 in Gregor et al. 2018); persistent profound microcephaly is consistently absent.

evidence.text: In a cohort of 21 individuals with pathogenic FBXO11 variants, mild intellectual disability occurred in 86%, facial dysmorphism in 67%, hypotonia in 62%, and behavioral dysregulation in 62%. Microcephaly was present in only 24%, seizures occurred in 43%, and neuroimaging abnormalities were nonspecific without progressive neurodegeneration or complex structural defects.

source.title: Defining FBXO11-Related Neurodevelopmental Disorder: Clinical, Molecular and Facial Assessment of 21 Patients
source.quote: Microcephaly occurred in 24%, while seizures were present in 43%. Brain imaging abnormalities were nonspecific and did not consistently correlate with epilepsy.

evidence.text: In 20 individuals with de novo variants in FBXO11, developmental delay was present in all, with microcephaly in 4/19, macrocephaly in 2/19, behavioral problems in 17/20, seizures in 5/20, and cleft lip/palate in 3/20. No complex congenital heart defects, limb reduction deficiencies, or neurodegeneration were reported.

source.title: De novo variants in the F-box protein FBXO11 in 20 individuals with a variable neurodevelopmental disorder
source.journal: The American Journal of Human Genetics
source.quote: They present with mild to severe developmental delay associated with a range of features including short (4/20) or tall (2/20) stature, obesity (5/20), microcephaly (4/19) or macrocephaly (2/19), behavioral problems (17/20), seizures (5/20), cleft lip or palate or bifid uvula (3/20), and minor skeletal anomalies.

evidence.text: In 12 affected individuals across 5 Chinese families with FBXO11 variants, core findings were intellectual disability (12/12), global developmental delay (10/12), and speech delay (8/12). Gross congenital malformations were completely absent across all 12 individuals.

source.title: FBXO11 variants are associated with intellectual disability and ...
source.quote: Distinguishingly, malformation was not observed in all the affected individuals.

evidence.text: Characterization of 2 individuals with de novo FBXO11 mutations revealed mild ID and postnatal mild microcephaly or borderline small head circumference alongside hyperactivity, rather than profound congenital microcephaly.

source.title: De novo FBXO11 mutations are associated with intellectual disability and behavioural anomalies
source.quote: Individual 1, a 14-year-old boy, has mild ID as well as mild microcephaly... start the delineation of the associated clinical picture which may also comprise postnatal microcephaly or borderline small head size and behavioural anomalies.

evidence.text: A cohort of 23 additional individuals with de novo FBXO11 variants confirmed that core manifestations are developmental delay, intellectual disability, behavioral anomalies, hypotonia, and facial dysmorphisms, noting that microcephaly and short stature occur in a minority but are more common than macrocephaly.

source.title: De novo missense variants in FBXO11 alter its protein expression and subcellular localization
source.quote: The phenotypic spectrum remains highly variable, with developmental delay and/or intellectual disability as the core feature and behavioral anomalies, hypotonia and various facial dysmorphism as frequent aspects.

conflicts: While profound/severe microcephaly is reliably absent, mild microcephaly is actually somewhat more frequent (21-24%) than macrocephaly (~10%) when abnormal head circumference occurs, meaning head circumference is predominantly normal rather than macrocephalic.

new_directions.question_text: What is the exact incidence and severity grade of cardiac and structural visceral defects across pooled international FBXO11 cohorts?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying whether subclinical cardiac abnormalities exist on formal echocardiographic screening will strengthen the use of cardiac structural integrity as an exclusion criterion.

new_directions.question_text: Does longitudinal tracking of head circumference trajectories from birth into adulthood show progressive deceleration or stabilization in FBXO11-mutated patients?
new_directions.rationale: Documenting head circumference Z-scores over time would formalize head growth parameters for differential diagnosis against primary microcephaly syndromes.
